Job Advert
This role is term time, which means that the gross annual salary advertised will be reduced proportionately based on the number of weeks worked during the academic year. Term time employees are contracted to work 38 weeks per year.
Please note that the full time equivalent for this position is 37 hours, so roles advertised with contracted hours less than 37 will be classed as part time. The gross annual salary advertised will be reduced based on the part time hours.
About the role
Do you enjoy helping children feel settled, safe, and included?
Working as a
Lunchtime Assistant
at
Cronk-y-Berry School
, you’ll take the lead during one of the busiest parts of the school day. You’ll be based in the dining hall and out in the playground, keeping things running smoothly - supporting pupils, stepping in when needed and setting clear expectations around behaviour, safety and respect. It’s a hands-on role where your presence makes a noticeable difference.
Working closely with colleagues, you’ll support staff in creating a calm, structured lunchtime, helping to ensure a positive and consistent experience for pupils. No formal qualifications are needed - just a steady approach, good judgement, and the confidence to engage with children and colleagues alike.
If you’re reliable, practical, and ready to be part of a school team, we’d like to hear from you!

jobs.department: Isle of Man Financial Services Authority
jobs.location: Finch Hill House (Isle of Man Financial Services Authority)
jobs.fullDescription:
Job Reference:
IOMF-024717
Salary:
£38,500 - £63,500
Closing Date:
21/06/2026
Department:
Isle of Man Financial Services Authority
Location:
Finch Hill House (Isle of Man Financial Services Authority)
Employment Type:
Permanent
Hours Per Week:
37
Job Advert
The Isle of Man Financial Services Authority (“the Authority”) regulates firms engaged in financial activities, including insurance, pensions, banking, investments, fiduciary services and fund administration. The Authority is also responsible for supervision of anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance for those involved in the financial sector as well as a range of other Designated Businesses, and oversight of compliance with the Beneficial Ownership Act 2017.
INVESTIGATOR - ENFORCEMENT & INTELLIGENCE DIVISION
The Authority is seeking an Investigator within the Enforcement & Intelligence Division. This is an interesting time to join the Authority to help us deliver our objectives which include an updated approach to supervision and oversight, enhanced data management and analytics, and the reduction of financial crime. The successful candidate will be an enthusiastic team player who can demonstrate the following attributes:
Strong relevant regulatory/industry practical experience in the fields of regulatory enforcement, compliance, risk, audit and/or forensic accounting.
Ideally experience of working on complex investigations, inspections or assurance work in the context of financial services enforcement and/or in a professional disciplinary context.
Highly analytical, able to interpret large volumes of complex information quickly and accurately and the ability to make logical and timely decisions.
Ability to work under pressure, manage a workload of varied complexity, to manage competing priorities and to deliver against deadlines.
Hold or be willing to work towards, a relevant professional qualification relating to investigative practice, risk, compliance, law, accounting or AML/CFT.
This is an exceptional opportunity within a people focused organisation and applicants seeking flexible working arrangements are welcome.
The right candidate will bring the above skills and experience and in return working at the Authority will provide candidates with the opportunity to:
Contribute to the development of the Isle of Man’s financial system;
Play an important role in the delivery of the Isle of Man Financial Services Authority’s diverse and important mandate;
Assist with the delivery of strategically important supervision work as part of a highly professional team;
Build a fulfilling career, reaching your full potential and feeling valued in an environment that supports diversity and inclusion;
Be part of a dynamic team where no two days are the same.
Special Requirement:
The post holder may have access to material of a secret, private and sensitive nature. Consequently, the post holder of this role will be required to be checked in order to hold and maintain a national security clearance level (SC). Any offer letter will be made subject to successful SC vetting status being achieved. The SC Vetting procedure involves enquiries about the post holder’s personal and private circumstances.
Our package includes:
Competitive salary
Defined benefit pension
Support for professional studies
25 days annual leave
Flexible working scheme
For a full job description and to apply please see the attachments linked below.
Closing date for applications is 21 June 2026
The Authority is an equal opportunities employer
Isle of Man Financial Services Authority ∙ P O Box 58 ∙ Finch Hill House ∙ Bucks Road ∙ Douglas ∙ IM99 1DT

Consultant Psychiatrist

CAMHS services on the Isle of Man are currently undergoing an exciting and innovative transformation. Recent initiatives include the launch of the TALK service, The THRIVE Model and a recent strategic waiting list project. This new position reflects the increased need for psychiatrist support across this genre, specifically following the recent implementation of a innovative new single point of access service within CAMHS.
The clinical work for this position will be split between providing clinical leadership to the CAMHS multidisciplinary team and direct patient care. As per the sample job plan in the attached job description, SPA time will be provided. This service has a well-developed MDT & allocations process, and the successful candidate will play an important leadership role in this alongside senior non-medical colleagues. The post holder will frequently provide consultant level clinical supervision to the other doctors in the team which includes one Associate Specialist and two Specialty Doctors.
It is a critical time for CAMHS services on the island and the post holder will have an exciting opportunity to influence, clinically lead and shape CAMHS services strategically, working with other colleagues to deliver excellence for children on the island.

About the role
We are seeking an experienced HR Adviser to join our HR team on a 12-month, fixed-term contract. The role will take the lead in providing a comprehensive HR service for the Office of the Clerk of Tynwald.
As a small parliamentary office, we seek proactive, motivated, and enthusiastic team players who are able passionate about their work with the acumen to be aware of the needs of the office. The right candidate will align with our core values and contribute positively to our culture.
The HR Adviser will manage the entire HR lifecycle, acting as the central point of contact and expertise on all HR matters. You will be responsible for implementing and maintaining all HR processes, advising managers on people and leading the development initiatives in the office.
This is a highly operational role combining the ability to provide day-to-day support and offer high-quality people-relations advice. Working independently, you will require a proactive mindset to ensure policy compliance, take full ownership of end-to-end HR operational activities and lead on delivery of service. Your expertise and insights will be instrumental in developing and implementing strategies that develop and retain staff ensuring that the Office of the Clerk of Tynwald is viewed as a highly desirable employer.
Working with key stakeholders, including senior managers, staff, uni
on representatives and the Office of Human Reso
urces
in the Isle of Man Government, you will contribute to the delivery of the Clerk of Tynwald services and achievement of organisational goals (Statement of Purpose).
About the Office of the Clerk of Tynwald
The Office of the Clerk of Tynwald provides a wide range of parliamentary and administrative services. The Office is proud to deliver high-quality services to Tynwald and the public, and has a reputation for excellence both on and off the Isle of Man.
You will be joining a small, friendly and professional organisation of just over 30 people who work hard to deliver the wide range of services expected in a modern parliament.
Corporate and Engagement Services deliver high-quality, customer-focused administrative and facilities services to Tynwald Court, its Branches, Committees, Members and Clerks. It is a busy, quality-conscious division which combine the required work on governance and compliance with providing engagement and educational opportunities for both the Manx community and for those visiting the Island in a professional or personal capacity. The team is proud to have the responsibility for the organisation of the Tynwald Ceremony and related events. The provision of HR services for the management and staff of the Office of the Clerk of Tynwald also sits within this Service Area.
The work of this small office is varied, and flexibility and adaptability are key qualities of all staff. The post holder will be expected to contribute to other tasks, cover for other team members and, on occasion, assist with work in other areas of the Clerk of Tynwald’s Office to deliver the wide range of services expected in a modern parliament.

A competitive salary in line with Public Service Commission pay scales.

subject to meeting the needs of the office
.

This internship will give you the opportunity to develop your skills in a variety of areas and learn about how Tynwald works as a small, modern parliament. With the support of your colleagues, you will develop your knowledge of parliamentary procedure, the legislative and scrutiny process, and the politics of the Isle of Man.
You will be based in the Research and Scrutiny Support team, where you will be directly involved in supporting Members and Committees of Tynwald as they examine and challenge the work of Government. You will also contribute to tasks that support the running of business in plenary sittings and assist with other functions of Legislative Services as required. You may also have opportunities to get involved in the wider activities of the Office of the Clerk of Tynwald.
The Parliamentary Internship has been running since 2014. Former interns have gone on to careers in other parliaments, the civil service, other areas of the public sector, and legal services, both in the Isle of Man and further afield.
The internship will run from the start of October 2026 to the end of September 2027.
About the Office of the Clerk of Tynwald
The Office of the Clerk of Tynwald provides a wide range of parliamentary and administrative services. The office is proud to deliver high-quality services to Tynwald and the public, and has a reputation for excellence both on and off the Isle of Man.
You will be joining a small, friendly and professional organisation of just over 30 people who work hard to deliver the wide range of services expected in a modern parliament.
Research and Scrutiny Support sits within Legislative Services, the division responsible for the functions directly in support of the legislature. The Research and Scrutiny Support team provides parliamentary research and information services for Members and Committees; supports the clerking of the scrutiny Committees; and provides administrative services for all Committees of Tynwald. Other functions provided by Legislative Services include the administration of sittings of the House of Keys, Legislative Council, and Tynwald, the creation of the Official Report (Hansard), the Listen Live and Again service, and support for Private Members’ Bills.

A competitive salary in line with Public Service Commission pay scales.

.

Ready to develop a career in neonatal nursing within a supportive and evolving service?
An exciting new opportunity has arisen in the Integrated Women, Children and Families Care Group. The Neonatal Unit are looking for a passionate and motivated Registered Nurse/Midwife to join the team as a
Neonatal Staff Nurse
.
You’ll join a supportive team environment, building specialist skills in neonatal care while contributing to high standards of clinical practice. Delivering safe, effective care to sick and preterm babies, you’ll play a vital role in supporting their development and wellbeing, working closely with families and the wider multidisciplinary team.
This opportunity will enable the post holder to complete a structured education and training program:
FiN (Foundation in Neonates)
- This 6-month programme is the first element of the QiS (Qualified in Speciality) pathway. It provides nurses brand new to neonates with the foundation knowledge they require to progress through their QiS training. The programme comprises of 11 study days taking the form of blended learning, together with clinical experience in special care, high dependency and as a supernumerary placement within intensive care. Learners work through a competency book to evidence their learning and are fully supported by both the educators on the programme and the educators within the clinical environment.
Intensive Care Module
- On completion of the FiN, and following consolidation of the knowledge learnt, you will progress to
this module undertaken at either Salford University, Manchester University or John Moore’s University, Liverpool.
There will also be a requirement to spend up to 12 months in a UK tertiary Neonatal Unit to gain the relevant Intensive Care experience and consolidate learning, during which the Band 5 salary will be paid.
The successful candidate will need to commit to two years employment on the Neonatal Unit following completion of training.
You can find out more about the QiS pathway here:
https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/national-standards-for-neonatal-qualified-in-specialty-qis-education/

Job Advert
Isle of Man Mental Health Act 1998:
Second Opinion Appointed Doctors
The Department of Health and Social Care (‘the Department’) are currently seeking to add to the existing pool of Second Opinion Appointed Doctors (SOADs), with applications for the unique role being welcomed until 31 October 2026.
If you are a qualified psychiatrist with at least 5 years’ practical experience at a senior level, then this could be an opportunity for you.
About the Isle of Man
The Isle of Man is a British Crown Dependency, located in the middle of the Irish Sea. As a Crown Dependency the Isle of Man has its own government that upholds laws and regulations, with an NHS style health care system.
Whilst the island does not fall under the jurisdiction or scrutiny of the NHS and CQC, we adopt the same or similar methodology and good practice as evidenced in the UK.
The easiest routes to get to the Isle of Man are via London airports, or transport links in the Northwest (air and sea).
Mental Health
The island has its own Mental Health Act 1998 (‘the Act’), which is based on the UK’s Mental Health Act 1983.
This includes safeguards for people who are covered by the powers of the Act, which describes the responsibilities of the Responsible Medical Officer or doctor and in what circumstances a second opinion for treatment should be sought from an independent Psychiatrist (SOAD).
SOADs are appointed by the Department, however interviews are undertaken by the local Mental Health Commission.
Reporting and accountability
The SOADs will report through the Head of Quality and Compliance at the Department of Health and Social Care.
The role and requirements from applicants
The pool of SOADs registered with the Department are completely independent of local services and work as and when requested. This is generally between 4 to 6 times per year, usually for one day each time. However, you may need to see up to 3 patients per visit.
The SOADs are called upon to provide second opinions for a patient’s treatment, where that patient is covered by the powers of the Act.
To fulfil this role, you must be able to meet the following criteria:
Qualified Psychiatrist, with at 5 years’ experience of clinical practice in a senior role
General Medical Council (GMC) registered – Please include your reference number
Hold a GMC Specialist registration
Member of the Royal College of Psychiatrists or have an equivalent qualification recognised by the Royal College of Psychiatrists.
Registered in good standing for Continued Professional Development.
Knowledge and experience of the Mental Health Act 1983 (England and Wales)
Experience in working with patients in acute hospital settings.
The Department offers an excellent remuneration package which includes travel and associated expenses.
Equality and Diversity
The Isle of Man Public Service is committed to creating an inclusive culture that celebrates
equality, diversity and inclusion
. We understand how a wide range of views and experiences can benefit us as we work together for the Isle of Man.
For further information and to apply, please contact Jade McCormick, Quality and Compliance team, Department of Health and Social Care at
jade.mccormick@gov.im
